newsitem.title: SPAIN: DIVING-ZHUPINA, WELS LEAD WAY AT EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: DIVING-ZHUPINA, WELS LEAD WAY AT EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Olympic highboard silver medallist Annika Walter was upstaged by Ukraine's Elena Zhupina but fellow German Andreas Wels staked a strong claim for the first gold medal of the European swimming championships in the men's one-metre springboard diving on Wednesday.

Zhupina, bronze medallist at the 1993 European championships in Sheffield, England, amassed 278.49 points from her five dives from the 10-metre platform in the preliminary round under a scorching sun at the San Pablo pool.
Walter, silver medallist at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics behind China's apparently invincible Fu Mingxia, had to settle for second spot with 267.45 ahead of German team mate Anke Piper ( 243.00).
All 17 entrants dive again on Thursday, taking Wednesday's points into a semifinal round to decide the 12 for the final the same day.
Wels, fourth at the last European championships in Vienna in 1995, heavily outscored his rivals on the one-metre springboard, compiling 342.21 points from his six dives.
Rafael Alvarez and Jose Luis Hidalgo raised the medal hopes of host nation Spain, finishing second and third with respective totals of 323.10 and 321.90.
The top 12 qualified for Thursday morning's semifinal round, which will be contested in two groups of six.
The top three in each semifinal vie for the first gold medal of the 12-day championships on Thursday afternoon before the women contest the 10-metre final.

The diving programme has been extended this year to include the innovation of four synchronised diving events. Teams of two will contest separate men's and women's titles from the three- metre and 10-metre boards.
Russia's Olga Sedakova made a confident start to her bid for a fourth successive synchronised swimming solo title with the highest marks in the technical programme preliminary round.
Sedakova scored 97.800 points to lead from Virginie Dedieu of France (95.880) and Giovanna Burlando of Italy (93.800).
The opening day's action comprised diving, water polo and synchronised swimming.
The main swimming events begin next Tuesday.
